A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched despite v2's additions and reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1–4 report original selective-classification experiments and ablations using DFN CLIP, EVA, and DistilBERT.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SIRC comparisons, ResNet50 and semantic-shift evaluations, sample-efficiency experiments, and hyperparameter-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The Δ-MDS and Δ-KNN scoring rules, averaged top-k implementation, linear combinations, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Expanded descriptions and tuning guidance do not establish a change to the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet-1K, six covariate-shift variants, and Amazon Reviews. v2 retains these and adds semantic-shift evaluations on ImageNet-O, iNaturalist, SUN, and Places relative to ImageNet-1K (Table 8), extending coverage to unseen-class conditions.

E2.justification: SIRC is newly evaluated alongside the retained comparators in the CLIP, EVA, and DistilBERT experiments (v2 Tables 1–3). Other newly cited approaches, such as trust scores and ViM, are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a ResNet50 trained solely on ImageNet-1K, varies labeled reference-data fractions from 0.1% to 100%, and sweeps λ and k (Tables 5 and 7; Figure 2). These substantially expand experimental controls and settings. Existing evaluation metrics, corruption severity, model configurations, and tabulated hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: The original neighbor-averaging and score-combination ablations remain in Table 4. v2 adds analyses of hyperparameter sensitivity, labeled-data efficiency, and whether gains persist with ImageNet-only pretraining, addressing practical and robustness questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. v2 retains point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in v1 Tables 1–4 are retained after matching the renumbered tables. v2 adds SIRC scores, ResNet50 and semantic-shift results, and sample-efficiency and sensitivity findings. For example, Table 5 reports Δ-KNN-RLog AURC of 4.81 with 0.1% labeled data versus 3.98 with 100%, extending the evidence under different data conditions.

T1.justification: The Neyman–Pearson lemma and corollary, Theorems 1–3, Lemma 2, and their proofs are substantively unchanged. v1 Appendices A–B become v2 Appendices B–C, retaining the averaged-neighbor argument. The new baseline formulas provide standard explanatory detail.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions concerning the Neyman–Pearson framework, two distance-based selectors, and their combinations remain. Introduction contribution 3 now explicitly claims evaluation under both covariate and semantic shifts, and the conclusion removes its covariate-only qualification.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies that correctness-conditioned densities encompass ID and shifted inputs together and that theoretical assumptions explain optimality rather than prescribe practical conditions. It interprets the ResNet50 experiment as countering a pretraining explanation and adds concrete low-data limitations: Δ-MDS degrades at 1% and is inapplicable at 0.1%, while Δ-KNN remains competitive. The main existing mechanism interpretations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix A documents Energy's temperature, KNN feature normalization, and SIRC's MSP/L1 combination and parameter fitting. v2 also adds λ/k selection guidance, identifies the ResNet50 source, and states that supplementary code includes instructions. Existing pseudocode, public code link, hardware, model variants, and hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of SIRC/SCOD through Xia and Bouganis (2022) and Narasimhan et al. (2024), trust scores through Jiang et al. (2018), and complementary logit/feature information through Wang et al. (2022). It contrasts its joint correctness-based formulation with separate ID/OOD modeling. The hallucination-survey citation is removed, while the principal positioning relative to Liang et al. remains.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related work and the conclusion, rearranges some experimental discussion, adds baseline explanations and ethics/reproducibility/LLM-use statements, and switches to author-year citations. The core section sequence and most method and proof exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds sample-efficiency Table 5, ResNet50 Table 7, semantic-shift Table 8, and sensitivity Figure 2. It moves the existing risk-coverage plots from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 3, redistributes existing tables, adds SIRC rows, and adopts ICLR headers and typography. Together these substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The new data-efficiency and sensitivity studies clarify practical requirements, while the ResNet50 control and SIRC comparison strengthen empirical support beyond v1. These benefits are tempered by reporting flaws in the additions: Table 7 highlights Δ-MDS-RLog as best on Im-S despite MSP's lower AURC (23.4 versus 24.1), and Table 8 contains unexplained EVA AURC/NAURC rank reversals under Equation 7. The added validation therefore supports a limited overall improvement.
